one_liner: Vonage offers self-serve communications APIs (Messages/SMS, Voice, Verify, Video) with free signup, API key/secret Basic auth and JWT auth; OAuth 2.0 exists for Business Communications and Network Features APIs; vendor MCP server exists only as documentation MCP.
auth_notes: Core APIs: API key+secret (Basic header) and self-minted JWT (app ID + private key). Vonage Business Communications APIs use OAuth 2.0 authorization code (and password grant) with consumer key/secret generated in the developer portal. Network Features use a CAMARA CIBA OAuth flow started with a JWT. OAuth is not the main path for core Messages/Voice/Video APIs, so OAUTH2 as primary applies to VBC only; core multi-user toolkit would likely use per-customer key/secret or JWT.
access_notes: Homepage invites visitors to create a free account; an API key and secret are created automatically with the account. Network Features need operator approval for production via Network Registry.
blocker_notes: Core APIs are self-serve with per-customer credentials. Network Features require operator approval for production. The MCP server is only supported by the registry signal (vendor namespace io.github.Vonage/vonage-documentation-mcp), not by fetched pages, and appears to be a documentation MCP.

evidence.quote: Ready to start building? Create a free account now!
When you create a Vonage account, an API key and secret will be created for you.
The OpenAPI specification for the Network Feature auth endpoints is available [here](/api/camara/auth).
